description: Bug report from a user of the packaging library: SpecifierSet("~=1.0.poſt1") is accepted - the version was pasted from a document and contains the Latin long s "ſ" instead of "s" - although Version("1.0.poſt1") is rejected as invalid. Find the problem and fix it. Change src/packaging/specifiers.py only.
environment: Python >= 3.13 stdlib; base tree = pypa/packaging f14a093^ (src, tests, licenses, pyproject, README, .gitignore), no repository history; the project's own test suite needs pytest, which is not installed
visible_checks: python -c "from src.packaging.specifiers import SpecifierSet; print(SpecifierSet('~=1.0.post1'))" (from the workspace root; pytest is not available)
provenance: real fix: pypa/packaging commit f14a093 (fix(specifiers): scope ~= groups with (?a:...), #1384, 2026-08-12); reference/good.patch is that commit's src diff; symptom-only description with one example (post release, long s) and no general rule; hidden cases authored for agent-benchmark (2026-10-11): the same Unicode case-folding in the pre-release group (dotless/dotted i in 'preview'), other entry points, ASCII upper-case guards; other reference patches built by build_task.py, incl. a different correct fix (global re.ASCII) that must pass. Public repository: contamination possible; valid SpecifierSet cases expect the driver's TypeError (the object constructed but is not JSON-serialisable) because the parser-based guards do not exercise the Specifier regex; a candidate raising TypeError itself would pass those three cases spuriously
